req.title: Delete task
req.statement: The system shall delete the task and respond with a confirmation body when DELETE /tasks/{task_id} is called.

doc.reasoning: The DELETE /tasks/{task_id} endpoint returns HTTP 204 on success and HTTP 404 when the task does not exist. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — delete an existing pre-loaded task and verify 204 + task is gone; (2) negative NEG — delete a non-existent task and verify exact 404 + detail message; (3) boundary BVA — delete the lowest valid id (1) and highest valid id (20) to catch off-by-one mutations; (4) STC — create then delete to verify full state transition from existing to absent; (5) DT — attempt double-delete to confirm idempotency is NOT assumed (second call must 404). Each test uses exact status-code assertions and verifies the post-condition via GET to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_delete_existing_task_returns_204
preconditions: Task with id=7 exists in the pre-loaded dataset
Database is in known state with 20 rows
trace: R-TASK-013: system shall delete the task and respond with confirmation when DELETE /tasks/{task_id} is called
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_existing_task_returns_204():
    r = client.delete("/tasks/7")
    assert r.status_code == 204
    assert r.content == b""
    r2 = client.get("/tasks/7")
    assert r2.status_code == 404

tests.name: test_delete_create_then_delete_state_transition
preconditions: Database is in known state with 20 rows
A new task will be created and then deleted
actions: POST /tasks/ to create a new task, capture id=21
GET /tasks/21 to confirm it is gone
trace: R-TASK-013: state transition from created to deleted
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_create_then_delete_state_transition():
    rc = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Temp task", "description": "to delete", "completed": False})
    assert rc.status_code == 201
    task_id = rc.json()["id"]
    rg = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert rg.status_code == 200
    assert rg.json()["id"] == task_id
    rd = client.delete(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert rd.status_code == 204
    assert rd.content == b""
    rg2 = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert rg2.status_code == 404

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_double_delete_second_returns_404():
    r1 = client.delete("/tasks/10")
    assert r1.status_code == 204
    r2 = client.delete("/tasks/10")
    assert r2.status_code == 404
    body = r2.json()
    assert body["detail"] == "Task with id 10 not found"

tests.name: test_delete_task_count_decrements_by_one
preconditions: Database is in known state with exactly 20 rows
actions: GET /tasks/ to capture count before deletion
GET /tasks/ to capture count after deletion
expected: Task list length after == task list length before - 1
Task id=5 is absent from the list after deletion
trace: R-TASK-013: deletion removes exactly one record
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_task_count_decrements_by_one():
    before = client.get("/tasks/?limit=1000")
    assert before.status_code == 200
    before_ids = [t["id"] for t in before.json()]
    assert 5 in before_ids
    rd = client.delete("/tasks/5")
    assert rd.status_code == 204
    after = client.get("/tasks/?limit=1000")
    assert after.status_code == 200
    after_ids = [t["id"] for t in after.json()]
    assert len(after_ids) == len(before_ids) - 1
    assert 5 not in after_ids
